title: The Quran: Surah 55, ar-Rahman (The Compassionate)
author: Tradução inglesa de Talal Itani (ClearQuran)
tradition: Texto sagrado do Islão, século VII
intro: Lição sobre a Surata 55. O texto inglês é a tradução de Talal Itani, reproduzida sem alterações; as notas de língua, perguntas, discussão e escrita são material pedagógico separado, baseado apenas no que o próprio texto diz. Cada nível estuda um excerto diferente.

source.title: Quran English Translation: Clear, Pure, Easy to Read Modern English
source.edition: Edition A (uses the word 'Allah' to refer to the Creator)

questions.q: According to verse 4, what did He teach man?
questions.why: O versículo 4 diz que Ele ensinou ao homem 'clear expression'.

questions.q: 'Maintain the weights with justice' (verse 9) is closest to:
options: Sell things at a high price
questions.why: 'Weights' são pesos e 'justice' é justiça; o versículo pede que se use o peso de forma justa.

questions.q: Verses 5 to 7 mention the sun, the moon, the stars, the trees and the sky. What do these verses suggest?
options: That the world follows an order, with a plan and a balance
That the sun is bigger than the earth
questions.why: O versículo 5 fala de 'according to plan' e o versículo 7 diz que Ele 'set up the balance'.

questions.q: What kind of sentence is verse 13?
questions.why: O versículo 13 é uma pergunta: 'So which of your Lord’s marvels will you deny?'

questions.q: Which sentence best sums up verses 10 to 12?
options: The earth is covered by sea
The earth is set up for the creatures and holds fruits, palms, grains and fragrant plants
questions.why: Os versículos 10 a 12 dizem que a terra foi posta para as criaturas e nomeiam frutos, palmeiras, grãos e plantas perfumadas.

B2.discussion: Verse 13 asks a question instead of making a statement. Why might a text ask its reader a question like this?
B2.writing: Write 80 to 100 words: Describe what the verses say about the sky, the earth and the balance.

questions.q: From what was man created, according to verse 14?
questions.why: O versículo 14 diz que o homem foi criado 'from hard clay, like bricks'; a fusão de fogo é a origem dos jinn (versículo 15).

questions.q: In verse 20, 'a barrier, which they do not overrun' means that the two seas:
options: do not cross the barrier between them
questions.why: 'Overrun' é ultrapassar; os dois mares não passam a barreira que os separa.

questions.q: Verse 24 says the ships are 'raised above the sea like landmarks'. What does the comparison suggest?
options: That the ships stand out on the sea, like markers you can see from far away
questions.why: Um 'landmark' é um ponto de referência que se destaca; a comparação sugere navios bem visíveis sobre o mar.

questions.q: How many times does the refrain 'So which of your Lord’s marvels will you deny?' appear in verses 14 to 25?
questions.why: A pergunta aparece nos versículos 16, 18, 21, 23 e 25, ou seja, cinco vezes.

questions.q: What is the effect of placing the refrain after each group of verses?
options: It changes the speaker each time
It adds new information each time
It divides the passage into short scenes and asks the same question after each one
questions.why: A mesma pergunta volta depois de cada imagem (barro, fogo, mares, pérolas, navios) e separa o texto em pequenas cenas.

C1.discussion: The same question returns after different images (clay, fire, seas, pearls, ships). What does the repetition do to the way the reader takes in these images?
C1.writing: Write 120 to 150 words: Explain how the refrain and the images work together in verses 14 to 25.

questions.q: In which verse does the refrain 'So which of your Lord’s marvels will you deny?' first appear?
questions.why: Os versículos 1 a 12 não têm a pergunta; ela aparece pela primeira vez no versículo 13.

questions.q: In verse 8, 'transgress' in 'do not transgress in the balance' is closest to:
questions.why: 'Transgress' é ultrapassar o limite; o versículo 9 repete a ideia com 'do not violate the balance'.

questions.q: What do the words 'plan' (verse 5) and 'balance' (verses 7 to 9) have in common?
options: Both suggest order and fair measure in the way things are arranged
questions.why: 'According to plan' e 'set up the balance' apontam para ordem e medida justa.

questions.q: How does the rhythm of the passage change after verse 13?
options: The passage becomes a list of commands
The refrain is absent from verses 1 to 12 and then returns after short groups of verses
questions.why: Depois do versículo 13 a pergunta volta nos versículos 16, 18, 21, 23 e 25, em grupos curtos.

questions.q: Which statement is best supported by the passage as a whole?
options: It tells one story with one character
It moves from teaching and order to images of creation and the sea, and keeps asking the same question
It gives a list of legal rules
questions.why: Os versículos 1 a 9 falam de ensino, ordem e equilíbrio; os versículos 14 a 25 dão imagens de criação e de mares; a pergunta repete-se.

C2.discussion: The refrain works as a question but does not expect an answer in words. How does the passage prepare the ground for that question before it first appears in verse 13?
C2.writing: Write 150 to 200 words: Analyse how the refrain shapes the structure of verses 1 to 25, referring to specific verses and words.
